mars_berries.title: Clues to Wet History in Texture of a Martian Rock
mars_berries.description: This close-up view of a target rock called "Last Chance" was acquired by the microscopic imager on the arm of NASA's Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity on March 3, 2004, during the 39th Martian day, or sol, of Opportunity's work on Mars. The area covered in the view is about 2 inches (5 centimeters) across.  The embedded spherules evident in this image reminded researchers of berries in a muffin, so they were nicknam

mars_rocknest.title: Billion-Pixel View From Curiosity at Rock Nest, White-Balanced
mars_rocknest.description: This image from NASA Curiosity Mars rover shows Curiosity at the Rocknest site where the rover scooped up samples of windblown dust and sand.

mars_jezero_delta.title: Perseverance View of the Delta in Jezero Crater
mars_jezero_delta.description: From its landing site, "Octavia E. Butler Landing," NASA's Perseverance rover can see a remnant of a fan-shaped deposit of sediments known as a delta with its Mastcam-Z instrument. Scientists believe this delta is what remains of the confluence between an ancient river and a lake at Mars' Jezero Crater. The delta remnant is the raised area of dark brown rock in the middle ground this image acquired on Feb. 22, 2021.

mars_phoenix_ice.title: Ice on Mars - Now You See It
mars_phoenix_ice.description: This color image was acquired by the Surface Stereo Imager on NASA Phoenix Mars Lander on the 21st day of the mission, or Sol 20 June 15, 2008. It shows lumps of ice in the lower left corner of a trench nicknamed Dodo-Goldilocks.

mars_phoenix_soil.title: Rosy Red Soil in Phoenix Scoop
mars_phoenix_soil.description: Rosy Red Soil in Phoenix Scoop

mars_murray_buttes.title: Farewell to Murray Buttes Image 3
mars_murray_buttes.description: This view from the Mast Camera (Mastcam) in NASA's Curiosity Mars rover shows finely layered rocks within the "Murray Buttes" region on lower Mount Sharp.  The buttes and mesas rising above the surface in this area are eroded remnants of ancient sandstone that originated when winds deposited sand after lower Mount Sharp had formed. mars_olympus.title: Color Mosaic of Olympus Mons
mars_olympus.description: Color mosaic of Olympus Mons volcano on Mars from the Viking 1 Orbiter. The mosaic was created using images from orbit 735 taken 22 June 1978. Olympus Mons is about 600 km in diameter and the summit caldera is 24 km above the surrounding plains.

mars_skylights.title: Seven Possible Cave Skylights on Mars
mars_skylights.description: Seven Possible Cave Skylights on Mars

mars_yardangs.title: On the Beauty of Yardangs
mars_yardangs.description: Some geological materials (like solid rock) are incredibly tough, but others (like piles of volcanic ash) are quite soft. Some materials are soft enough that they can be eroded by the wind alone and yield landscapes that look like what we see in this HiRISE image. mars_ice_scarp.title: Underground Martian Ice Deposit Exposed at Scarp
mars_ice_scarp.description: Click on the image for larger version  A cross-section of a thick sheet of underground ice is exposed at the steep slope (or scarp) that appears bright blue in this enhanced-color view from the High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE) camera on NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. mars_dust_storm.title: Mars Dust Storm in Relation to InSight, Curiosity and Perseverance
mars_dust_storm.description: The beige clouds seen in this flat global map of Mars are a continent-size dust storm captured on Sept. 29, 2022 by the Mars Color Imager (MARCI) camera aboard NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO). As MRO passes over the planet, MARCI takes linear images – essentially strips – of the planet's circumference each day. The images are then stitched together to create a daily global map of the planet, showing atmosphe

mars_jezero_orbit.title: Jezero Crater as Seen by ESA's Mars Express Orbiter
mars_jezero_orbit.description: This image shows the remains of an ancient delta in Mars' Jezero Crater, which NASA's Perseverance Mars rover will explore for signs of fossilized microbial life. The image was taken by the High Resolution Stereo Camera aboard the ESA (European Space Agency) Mars Express orbiter. The European Space Operations Centre in Darmstadt, Germany, operates the ESA mission. The High Resolution Stereo Camera was developed by a

mars_dust_devil_hirise.title: Mars Whirling Dust Devil
mars_dust_devil_hirise.description: A Martian dust devil was captured winding its way along the Amazonis Planitia region of Northern Mars on March 14, 2012 NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

mars_opportunity_shadow.title: Opportunity Catches its Shadow on Sol 180
mars_opportunity_shadow.description: This self-portrait of NASA Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity comes courtesy of the Sun and the rover front hazard-avoidance camera. The dramatic snapshot of Opportunity shadow was taken as the rover continues to move farther into Endurance Crater

moon_marius_pit.title: Marius Hills Pit -- Lava Tube Skylight?
moon_marius_pit.description: The Marius Hills pit is a possible skylight in a lava tube in an ancient volcanic region of the Moon called the Marius Hills. This image was taken by NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.

moon_tycho.title: Tycho Crater's Peak
moon_tycho.description: NASA image release June 30, 2011  On June 10, 2011, NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter captured a dramatic sunrise view of Tycho crater.  A very popular target with amateur astronomers, Tycho is located at 43.37°S, 348.68°E, and is about 51 miles (82 km) in diameter. moon_far_side.title: Far Side of Moon Imaged by MoonKAM
moon_far_side.description: This image of the lunar surface was taken by NASA MoonKAM system onboard the Ebb spacecraft and shows Crater Poinsot located on the northern part of the moon far side.

moon_apollo17.title: Apollo 17 Mission image - Sta 6,Panoramic,LMP
moon_apollo17.description: AS17-140-21497 (13 Dec. 1972) --- Scientist-astronaut Harrison H. Schmitt is photographed standing next to a huge, split lunar boulder during the third Apollo 17 extravehicular activity (EVA) at the Taurus-Littrow landing site. moon_bootprint.title: KSC-as11-40-5877
moon_bootprint.description: JOHNSON SPACE CENTER, HOUSTON, TEXAS -- Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon July 20, 1969, and, after take-off from the Moon July 21, joined Collins in the Command Module circling the Moon.  The astronauts splashed down in the Pacific Ocean and recovery was made by the U.S.S. Hornet at 12:50 p.m. EDT, July 24, 1969.

earth_lanzarote.title: Lanzarote, Spanish Canary Islands
earth_lanzarote.credit: NASA/METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems, and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team
earth_lanzarote.description: Los Volcanes Natural Park on Lanzarote in the Spanish Canary Islands is serving as a training ground to prepare for the next mission to the Moon and Mars. NASA and ESA use it for astronaut training and testing Mars Rovers. Astronauts are taught to become effective field geologists and geo-microbiologists in a planetary science context. earth_dry_valleys.title: Dry Valleys, Antarctica
earth_dry_valleys.credit: NASA/GSFC/METI/ERSDAC/JAROS, and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team
earth_dry_valleys.description: The McMurdo Dry Valleys are a row of valleys west of McMurdo Sound, Antarctica. They are so named because of their extremely low humidity and lack of snow and ice cover. This image was acquired December 8, 2002 by NASA Terra spacecraft.

earth_afrera.title: Lake Afrera, Ethiopia
earth_afrera.credit: NASA/GSFC/METI/ERSDAC/JAROS, and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team
earth_afrera.description: Lake Afrera is a hypersaline lake located in the Danakil Depression in northern Ethiopia where rock salt has been mined for centuries. This image was acquired by NASA Terra spacecraft.

earth_salar_atacama.title: Salar de Atacama, Chile
earth_salar_atacama.credit: NASA/METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems, and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team
earth_salar_atacama.description: Salar de Atacama (Atacama salt flats) in Chile's Atacama Desert receives 2 mm rain per year. Its attraction are the brines 40 m below ground. They are pumped to the surface into large evaporation pans. After the water has vanished, a yellowish greasy solution is left behind that contains lithium.
